data.title: CoronaNet Research Project
data.long_description: The CoronaNet Research Project is an initiative spearheaded by researchers at NYU Abu Dhabi, Hochschule für Politik at the TU Munich, and Yale University to compile data on government responses to the COVID-19 pandemic. The initial hand-coded dataset—assembled in cooperation with 500 political, social, and public health scholars from around the world—provides information on 15,000 separate policy announcement from governments beginning in 31 December. These actions are coded to indicate the level of government responding (e.g. national, regional, or local), the specific actions taken (e.g. travel bans, investments), geographic areas targeted, population or object targeted, compliance mechanism, and timing.

data.long_description: The Inter-American Development Bank and Citibeats are operating a citizen observatory to understand how people across Latin America and the Caribbean are responding to the current COVID-19 crisis. Researchers analyze and process tweets made by people mentioning COVID-19 who have also indicated their location on Twitter. Individuals can also anonymously leave comments via a survey. Researchers then use an artificial intelligence system to group collected comments into one of thirteen categories based on the concerns raised—including food security, economic security, education, and mental health—to determine what percent of respondents reported those concerns on a country-by-country basis. data.description: The company Unacast launched a COVID-19 Social Distancing Scorecard to help organizations measure efforts to limit mobility.
data.title: COVID-19 Social Distancing Scoreboard
data.long_description: The company Unacast, which collects and analyzes location data to understand human activity, launched a COVID-19 Social Distancing Scorecard to help organizations measure and understand the efficacy of US public health initiatives to limit mobility. The resource uses aggregated mobility data collected from smart devices as a proxy for whether people are remaining home and analyzes it on a state and county level, assigning letter grades based on changes in movement compared to what is typical for that area. States and counties with large decreases in movement are considered to be successful in their interventions. The maps are searchable and updated daily. It cannot identify whether people are staying more than six feet apart.

data.description: Professors at the University of Chicago published a piece in the opinion section of the New York Times demonstrating relative risks of COVID-19 infection by establishment type.
data.title: Is It Safer to Visit a Coffee Shop or a Gym?
data.long_description: Professors at the University of Chicago published a piece in the opinion section of the New York Times demonstrating relative risks of COVID-19 infection by establishment type. The researchers rely on aggregated cell phone data from the companies SafeGraph and Verasite to show the average length of a visitor to a business relative to the average square footage of the establishment. They also conducted a survey asking individuals to rate, on a scale of 1 to 10, how they interacted with people, how much they touched shared surfaces, and how much of the business’s activity took place outside. The researchers suggest gyms, sit-down restaurants, and bars should take caution in opening due to increased risk of spreading the virus.

data.long_description: Researchers with Microsoft Research, University College London, and Public Health England analyzed searches on Bing in England to identify possible cases of influenza-like illnesses like COVID-19. data.description: Raj Chetty and his colleagues published a working paper on the effects of COVID-19 and subsequent responses to it on the US economy.
data.title: How Did COVID-19 and Stabilization Policies Affect Spending and Employment? A New Real-Time Economic Tracker Based on Private Sector Data
data.long_description: Raj Chetty and his colleagues published a working paper on the effects of COVID-19 and subsequent responses to it on the US economy. The working paper relies on granular, real-time anonymized data collected from businesses to provide information on weekly consumer spending, business revenue, employment rates, and other information. data.long_description: Quandl, a financial services company that indexes numerical datasets, used its “alternative data” assets to assess the economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in China, Japan, and the United States. The company uses data from transit authorities, railway operators, telecommunications networks, and government briefings on consumer traffic to assess the impact of shelter-in-place directives, noting the orders led to substantial declines in movement. The analysis also uses time-tracking data from software companies like Homebase to measure the number of small-business closures. This analysis suggests roughly 65 percent of New York businesses closed in January 2020 while 50 percent of Texan businesses and 52 percent of Californian businesses did that same. data.long_description: The purpose of this repository is to collate data on the ongoing coronavirus pandemic in Africa. The data will be obtained from official sources (e.g., WHO, departments of health, CDC etc.) and unofficial sources (e.g., news). The organizers maintain an open-access database of COVID-19 related research that spans topics such as biomedicine, lifesciences, engineering, physical sciences, sociology, economics, behavioral, and cultural issues. This database can be searched to help funders and researchers understand which topics are currently being studied.
data.participants: University of Birmingham, UKCDR, Academy of Medical Sciences, Academy of Social Sciences Campaign for Social Justice, GLOPID-R, CanCOVID, COVID-19 Social Science Research Tracker
data.short_description: COVID CORPUS is a collaborative effort by researchers to compile their activity on COVID-19 around the world to reduce the possibility of duplication.

data.description: The international development networking platform Devex manages a dashboard of international funding directed toward COVID-19 response.
data.title: Devex Funding the Response to COVID-19 Visualization

thumbnail.filename_download: img/Devex Funding the Response to COVID-19 Visualization.png
thumbnail.title: Devex Funding The Response To Covid 19 Visualization

data.long_description: The international development networking platform Devex manages a dashboard of international funding directed toward COVID-19 response since 1 January. The visualization, which runs on Tableau’s data visualization software, displays global funding by country, funder type, and focus area based on data input to the Devex site. Individuals can use the platform to conduct basic funding analysis.

data.short_description: The international development networking platform Devex manages a dashboard of international funding directed toward COVID-19 response.

data.description: Cities and Memory is collecting sound recordings from around the world to understand how the COVID-19 pandemic has affected soundscapes around the world.
data.title: Cities and Memory #StayHomeSounds
data.long_description: Cities and Memory, a collaborative field-recording sound project, is collecting sound recordings from around the world to understand how the COVID-19 pandemic has affected soundscapes around the world. Individuals can submit sounds and stories from the COVID-19 lockdown from their home. The work is a facet of a larger effort that includes more than 4,000 sounds across 100 countries and territories.
data.participants: Stuart Fowkes
data.short_description: Cities and Memory is collecting sound recordings from around the world to understand how the COVID-19 pandemic has affected soundscapes around the world.

data.description: The consortium compiles electronic health records across 202 hospitals and 12 health systems to answer questions about COVID-19.
data.title: COVID-19 Data Discovery from Clinical Records Consortium

thumbnail.filename_download: img/COVID-19 Data Discovery from Clinical Records Consortium.png
thumbnail.title: Covid 19 Data Discovery From Clinical Records Consortium

data.long_description: The COVID-19 Data Discovery from Clinical Records Consortium is a network of 202 hospitals across 12 health systems that compiles electronic health record data to help researchers address complex clinical questions related to COVID-19. To better preserve patient and institutional privacy, the consortium does not share individual records but instead exchanges aggregate statistics to inform medical research.
data.participants: UC San Diego, UC Davis Health, UTHealth, University of Southern California, San Mateo Medical Center, University of Colorado, Ludwig-Maximilians-Universitat Munchen, Cedars Sinai; University of California San Francisco, University of California Los Angeles, Vanderbilt University
data.short_description: The consortium compiles electronic health records across 202 hospitals and 12 health systems to answer questions about COVID-19.

data.description: Researchers developed a tool to detect and predict outbreak spread at a county level in the United States
data.title: COVID-19 Outbreak Detection Tool
data.long_description: Using machine-learning methods, researchers at Massachusetts General Hospital, Harvard Medical School, Georgia Tech and Boston Medical Center developed a tool to detect and predict outbreak spread at a county level in the United States.  The tool relies on officially reported COVID-19 cases and deaths as well as factors like mask mandates, social distancing policies, and the CDC’s Social Vulnerability Index. Data updates two-to-three times per week and the tool visualizes all findings on a publicly available county map of the United States.
data.participants: Massachusetts General Hospital, Harvard Medical School, Georgia Tech, Boston Medical Center
data.short_description: Researchers developed a tool to detect and predict outbreak spread at a county level in the United States

data.description: Nextstrain is a project to track the evolution of pathogens around the globe to aid in epidemiological research and outbreak response.
data.title: Nextstrain SARS-CoV-2 Research
data.long_description: Nextstrain is an inter-institutional, open source project to track the evolution of pathogens around the globe to aid in epidemiological research and outbreak response. Amid the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, the Nextstrain research team has analyzed data on SARS-CoV-2 by region and published regular updates on its genomic epidemiology work.
data.participants: Fred Hutch, Max Planck Institute for Developmental Biology, National Institutes of Health, Mapbox, European Research Council, Open Science Prize, Biozentrum
data.short_description: Nextstrain is a project to track the evolution of pathogens around the globe to aid in epidemiological research and outbreak response.

data.description: The Citizens and Technology Lab at Cornell University has developed a service monitoring the algorithms on the social media platform Reddit during the COVID-19 pandemic.
data.title: COVID-19 Reddit Algo-Tracker
data.long_description: The Citizens and Technology Lab at Cornell University has developed a service monitoring the algorithms on the social media platform Reddit, taking snapshots every two-to-three minutes. During the COVID-19 pandemic, Cornell is using its service to better understand communication during the pandemic, collecting posts that use coronavirus-related, English-language terms. The work will inform the Citizens and Technology Lab’s collaborations with Reddit communities. It will also help the lab understand the role ranking algorithms play on public discourse. Results from the collection are displayed with visualiztions available on the tracker’s website.
data.contact_info: Dr. J. Nathan Matias, Citizens and Technology Lab
data.participants: Citizens and Technology Lab, Reddit
data.short_description: The Citizens and Technology Lab at Cornell University has developed a service monitoring the algorithms on the social media platform Reddit during the COVID-19 pandemic.

data.description: Yelp is gathering data from listings on its site to understand the effects of COVID-19 on businesses across the country.
data.title: Understanding the effects of COVID-19 on businesses across the country using Yelp Data
data.long_description: Yelp is using data gathered from listings on the site to understand the effects of COVID-19 on businesses across the country. In July and September 2020, it released Local Economic Impact Reports to generate insight on where, when, and how businesses were impacted by the pandemic. For example, the September 2020 report showed that businesses that provided home, local, or professional services were able to withstand the effects of the pandemic better than expected.
data.participants: Yelp
data.short_description: Yelp is gathering data from listings on its site to understand the effects of COVID-19 on businesses across the country.

data.description: A WhatsApp-facilitated study sought to identify the number of treatment delays in cancer patients with COVID-19, mistakes made within the hospital system, and the emotional levels of these patients.
data.title: Patients With Cancer and COVID-19: A WhatsApp Messenger-Based Survey of Patients’ Queries, Needs, Fears, and Actions Taken
data.long_description: This study was conducted in three oncology units in Italy, to understand fears and needs related to cancer patients with COVID-19. Over 446 Whatsapp messages were analyzed between March 1 and March 13 to understand the number of treatment delays in cancer patients, mistakes made within the hospital system, and the emotional levels of these patients.
data.participants: American Society of Clinical Oncology, GSTU Foundation and the Risk Management Unit, University of Palermo
data.short_description: A WhatsApp-facilitated study sought to identify the number of treatment delays in cancer patients with COVID-19, mistakes made within the hospital system, and the emotional levels of these patients

data.description: A  company aggregated foot traffic data in North America to visualizes the impact the pandemic has had on the US economy.
data.title: The impact of COVID-19 on foot traffic
data.long_description: Safegraph has aggregated foot traffic data in North America, with over 6 million points of interest (POI) across the country. This dashboard visualizes the impact the pandemic has had on the US economy and daily life by comparing data from recent months on commercial activity (foot traffic data) to that of previous years.
data.participants: Safegraph
data.short_description: A  company aggregated foot traffic data in North America to visualizes the impact the pandemic has had on the US economy.

data.description: This research study uses cell phone data to map the hourly movements of 98 million people to simulate the spread of COVID-19 in major cities.
data.title: Mobility network models of COVID-19 explain inequities and inform reopening
data.long_description: This research study uses cell phone data to map the hourly movements of 98 million people from neighborhoods to points of interests (such as restaurants or stores) and simulate the spread of COVID-19 in major metropolitan cities. The model is used to predict a variety of factors, including infection rates amongst disadvantaged socioeconomic and racial groups and key superspreader POIs. The study, ultimately, is intended to inform equitable policy response to COVID-19 across North America.
data.participants: Stanford University, Northwestern University, Cambridge University
data.short_description: This research study uses cell phone data to map the hourly movements of 98 million people to simulate the spread of COVID-19 in major cities.

data.description: The icovid project is an European Commission-funded research project to develop an AI that can better diagnose patients with suspected COVID-19 infections.
data.title: icovid
data.long_description: The icovid project is an European Commission-funded research project coordinated by the medical imaging company icometrix to develop an AI that can better diagnose patients with suspected COVID-19 infections. The project seeks to achieve this goal through the development of a CT diagnosis software, built using collections of thorax scans of patients with and without COVID-19. The final product will be able to quantify infections, quickly and objectively assess the lesion burden, and allow for better patient care.
data.participants: icometrix, King’s Colelge London, Vrije Universiteit Brussel/UZ Brussel, Universitätsklinikum Heidelberg, Centre Hospitalier Universitaire de Liège, Universite de Liege, University of Oxford, Maastricht University, The Medical Cloud Company
data.short_description: The icovid project is an European Commission-funded research project to develop an AI that can better diagnose patients with suspected COVID-19 infections.

data.description: DataLoch is aiding response to COVID-19 in southeast Scotland by helping produce linked datasets to support hospital-based service management.
data.title: COVID-19 Collaborative
data.long_description: DataLoch, a repository of health and social care data about Edinburgh and southeast Scotland, has been asked by NHS Lothian and the University of Edinburgh to aid regional response to COVID-19 by helping produce linked datasets to support hospital-based service management. The dataset, which requires an application to access, combines hospital laboratory information, electronic patient records, Scottish morbidity records, critical care audit and community prescribing information as well as information on testing, COVID-19 symptoms, and tests.
data.participants: DataLoch, NHS Lothian, University of Edinburgh
data.short_description: DataLoch is aiding response to COVID-19 in southeast Scotland by helping produce linked datasets to support hospital-based service management.

data.description: PERISCOPE is an European Commission-funded effort to “map and analyse the unintended impacts of the COVID-19 outbreak.”
data.title: PERISCOPE
data.long_description: PERISCOPE, a Pan-European Response to the ImpactS of COVID-19 and future Pandemics and Epidemics, is an effort from the University of Pavia and a consortium of 32 institutions to “map and analyse the unintended impacts of the COVID-19 outbreak.” The partners plan to bring together expertise on the clinical and epidemiological; socio-economic and political; and statistical and technological aspects of the pandemic. data.description: Corona Map is a student-built site built to visualize the spread of COVID-19 across South Korea using data collected from government and academic reports.
data.title: Corona Map
data.long_description: Corona Map is a site built by a student at Kyunghee University to visualize the spread of COVID-19 across South Korea using data collected from government and academic reports produced by South Korea, China, the United States, and the World Health Organization. The site displays the location of positive tests as well as statistics for cases to help South Korean residents assess relative risk in their area. The site is reportedly one of the leading sources of up-to-the-minute tallies of confirmed infections in Korea.

data.short_description: Corona Map is a student-built site built to visualize the spread of COVID-19 across South Korea using data collected from government and academic reports.

data.description: TELUS is sharing insights with NSERC researchers free of charge and providing supervised and guided access to strongly de-identified and aggregated network mobility data
data.title: TELUS Data for Good
data.long_description: The Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council (NSERC), the largest funder of natural science and engineering research in Canada, and TELUS are working together to support government efforts to flatten the curve and reduce the spread of COVID-19. TELUS will share insights with NSERC researchers free of charge and provide supervised and guided access to strongly de-identified and aggregated network mobility data to be used by NSERC-eligible researchers that are studying and assessing the COVID-19 crisis. For research projects that qualify, NSERC will offer a $50,000 grant as part of their NSERC Alliance COVID-19 grants program.

data.description: CrisisReady was a collaboration between the disaster relief nonprofit Direct Relief and other researchers to investigate the value of mobility data for COVID-19 response.
data.title: Digital Mobility Data, Physical Distancing, and COVID-19 in Syracuse

thumbnail.filename_download: img/Digital Mobility Data, Physical Distancing, and COVID-19 in Syracuse.png
thumbnail.title: Digital Mobility Data, Physical Distancing, And Covid 19 In Syracuse

data.long_description: CrisisReady was a collaboration between the disaster relief nonprofit Direct Relief, researchers at the Harvard School of Public Health, Harvard Medical School, Stanford University, and other researchers to investigate the value of mobility data for COVID-19 response. Using data gleaned by Harvard researchers from the COVID-19 Mobility Data Network and Facebook (access to both obtained by Harvard) and data analysts based in Syracuse, New York, researchers created an interactive dashboard that could be used by the Mayor of Syracuse and others to understand changes in movement in response to social distancing measures, reopenings, holidays, and temperature changes. The project ran from March through June and intended to demonstrate how large, data sources could provide value to emergency response.
data.participants: Facebook, Direct Relief, Harvard School of Public Health, Harvard Medical School, Stanford University
data.short_description: CrisisReady was a collaboration between the disaster relief nonprofit Direct Relief and other researchers to investigate the value of mobility data for COVID-19 response.

data.description: The COVID-19 Mobility Network Modeling initiative seeks to model the effect of different non-pharmeceutical interventions on the geographic distribution of COVID-19 infections.
data.title: COVID-19 Mobility Network Monitoring
data.long_description: The COVID-19 Mobility Network Modeling initiative is a Stanford PhD student-led research project that seeks to model the effect of different non-pharmeceutical interventions on the geographic distribution of COVID-19 infections.  The project relies on data from SafeGraph, a company that tracks human mobility using cell phone data, collected between March and May 2020 across 10 large US metro areas. The resulting simulation demonstrates how infections occur hour-by-hour. An associated user tool shows to the reader how different restrictions, such as limits on restaurant services, religious organizations, grocery stores, and fitness centers, impacts COVID-19 cases over time.
data.participants: Safegraph, Stanford University; Cornell Tech, Northwestern University
data.short_description: The COVID-19 Mobility Network Modeling initiative seeks to model the effect of different non-pharmeceutical interventions on the geographic distribution of COVID-19 infections.

data.description: The COVID-19 Mobility Project is an effort to use telecom data to improve understanding of changes in mobility throughout the COVID-19 pandemic.
data.title: COVID-19 Mobility Project
data.long_description: The COVID-19 Mobility Project is an effort from the Robert Koch Institute and Humboldt University of Berlin to use telecom data from the Deutsche Telekom (distributed by the company Motionlogic) and Telefónica (analyzed and aggregated by the mobility data company Teralytics) to improve understanding of changes in mobility throughout the COVID-19 pandemic. The project maintains a "mobility monitor" which displays daily changes in the number of trips across Germany from March onward. It also produces  reports describing major findings following notable changes.
data.participants: Robert Koch institute, Humboldt University of Berlin, Deutsche Telekom, Motionlogic, Telefonica
data.short_description: The COVID-19 Mobility Project is an effort to use telecom data to improve understanding of changes in mobility throughout the COVID-19 pandemic.

data.description: A World Bank research team used smartphone  data about Colombia, Mexico, and Indonesia to assess the impact of pandemic-related mobility restrictions on real-world human movements.
data.title: Uncovering socioeconomic gaps in mobility reduction during the COVID-19 pandemic using location data

thumbnail.filename_download: img/Uncovering socioeconomic gaps in mobility reduction during the COVID-19 pandemic using location data.png
thumbnail.title: Uncovering Socioeconomic Gaps In Mobility Reduction During The Covid 19 Pandemic Using Location Data

data.long_description: A World Bank research team used smartphone location data about Colombia, Mexico, and Indonesia, obtained from the mobility-data company Cuebiq, to assess the impact of pandemic-related mobility restrictions on real-world human movements. The research suggests that mobility restrictions contributed to declines in human mobility, particularly among those in the top decile of wealth. The piece suggests that further reducing disease spread requires allocating resources to respond to the needs of vulnerable socioeconomic groups.
data.participants: World Bank, Cuebiq
data.short_description: A World Bank research team used smartphone  data about Colombia, Mexico, and Indonesia to assess the impact of pandemic-related mobility restrictions on real-world human movements.

data.description: University researchers used Cuebiq data to highlight changes in mobility before, during, and after movement restrictions were imposed in Canada.
data.title: Mobility and Proximity in Canada During the COVID-19 Pandemic

thumbnail.filename_download: img/Mobility and Proximity in Canada During the COVID-19 Pandemic.png
thumbnail.title: Mobility And Proximity In Canada During The Covid 19 Pandemic

data.long_description: Mobility Proximity in Canada During the COVID-19 Pandemic is a report from the Innovation Policy Lab at the University of Toronto to highlight changes in mobility before, during, and after movement restrictions were imposed in Canada. Using anonymized cell phone data, the report is intended to support decision-makers in policy and public sector to understand the impacts of social distancing measures on Canadian life. The report found that while movement levels have been largely restored, proximity levels have not increased and Canadians continue to avoid interacting with others.
data.participants: Cuebiq, University of Toronto
data.short_description: University researchers used Cuebiq data to highlight changes in mobility before, during, and after movement restrictions were imposed in Canada.

data.long_description: The COVID-19 Research Database is a pro bono effort from a coalition of healthcare companies to provide researchers with real-world, de-identified data. data.description: Researchers created a data-driven user tool to help individuals in the United States assess the risk level of attending an event in their area given the event size and location.
data.title: COVID-19 Event Risk Assessment Planning Tool

thumbnail.filename_download: img/COVID-19 Event Risk Assessment Planning Tool.jpg
thumbnail.title: Covid 19 Event Risk Assessment Planning Tool

data.long_description: Researchers at the Georgia Institute of Technology, Applied Bioinformatics Laboratory, and Stanford University created a data-driven user tool to help individuals in the United States assess the risk level of attending an event in their area given the event size and location. Using publicly reported COVID-19 case counts from the New York Times, COVID Tracking Project, and public health officials and a model for disease spread developed in March, the core tool represents the risk that at least one COVID-19 positive person will attend an event in a given US county. Individuals can adjust the model according to event size and ascertainment bias (the assumption that there will be more cases than reported). The researchers have also developed a sister tool to represent risk in the United Kingdom, Spain, France, Italy, Switzerland, Austria, Slovenia, Denmark, and Sweden.

data.description: The International Monetary Fund released an analysis assessing the impact of COVID-19 and subsequent lockdown measures on economic activity.
data.title: IMF World Economic Outlook, October 2020
data.long_description: The International Monetary Fund released an analysis assessing the impact of COVID-19 and subsequent lockdown measures on economic activity. The analysis relies on real-time mobility data on 128 countries provided by Google and job posting data from the company Indeed to actas proxies for economic activity. From these assets, the researchers found significant drops in movement in high-income countries as well as declines in job postings. The analysis also used mobility data on Italy, Portugal, and Spain from the telecommunications company Vodafone. Their analysis of this data found that stay-at-home orders and school closures had greater effects on women than men (suggesting women bear much of the burden in childcare) and that younger people (18 to 24 and 25 to 44) more significantly reduced their mobility than older cohorts.

data.description: In a paper published in the journal Nature,  a group of researchers studied how online search-query data might support public health surveillance for COVID-19.
data.title: Tracking COVID-19 using online search
data.long_description: In a paper published in the journal Nature,  a group of researchers studied how online search-query data might support public health surveillance for COVID-19. The research relied on data obtained from Google Health Trends, a non-public application interface offered by Google to researchers to help them study search data; a collection of media coverage on COVID-19; and daily confirmed COVID-19 cases and deaths as reported by the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control. From an analysis of eight countries—the United States, United Kingdom, Australia, Canada, France, Italy, Greece, and South Africa—the researchers found online searches for COVID-19 terminology closely precede confirmed cases and deaths. They conclude that search data could help supplement existing public health surveillance approaches.

data.description: The United Nations Development Programme released a series of reports  examining the impact and implications of the pandemic across Equatorial Guinea, Liberia, South Sudan and Togo.
data.title: Assessment of impacts and implications of COVID-19 in Equatorial Guinea, Liberia, South Sudan, Togo
data.long_description: The United Nations Development Programme released a series of reports produced through a collaboration between the Data-Pop Alliance and four UNDP country offices in sub-Saharan Africa. Titled "Impacts and Implications of COVID-19 in Equatorial Guinea, Liberia, South Sudan and Togo," these reports examine the impact and implications of the pandemic across several affected countries. They use macroeconomic and fiscal analysis to understand the pandemic's socioeconomic consequences on the people of those countries and the impact of the crisis on progress toward the Sustainable Development Goals. This work will be supplemented by a forthcoming seven-country study focusing on disaster risk governance in the Sahel and Lake Chad region.

data.title: Effect of non-pharmaceutical interventions to contain COVID-19 in China
data.long_description: Using data provided by the Chinese search engine Baidu, this project measures the effectiveness of non-pharmaceutical interventions in response to COVID-19 across China. It analyzed first-party data capturing movement within and outside of cities, proximity and contact patterns, and the timeliness of disease reporting to construct daily travel networks and simulate likely outbreak scenarios. It then made these models, but not the underlying data, available to inform research and public decision-making.
